...We have conducted extensive research on Hoochief behaviors, compiled in this book. Below are excerpts from our observations, so that our readers can compare behavioral changes in Hoochiefs before and after exposure to toxic spores, as well as before and after improvements in the biological environment of the Dim Forest.
 
Hoochiefs Not Exposed to Toxic Spores:
Hoochiefs are a patriarchal, pack-oriented species with a strong territorial instinct. The core members of the pack lead them to collaborate in teams to repel any intruders from their domain.

Uninfected Hoochiefs can communicate with each other and use simple tools made of stones and sticks.

Hoochiefs Exposed to Toxic Spores:
Infected Hoochiefs develop grey eyes and exhibit anxious, erratic behaviors as the toxic spores infiltrate their bodies, resulting in frequent coughing and vomiting. They may also compulsively scratch and tear at their own backs. In the final stage of infection, each violent cough releases a mist of spores, making them highly contagious sources of infection.

Infected Hoochiefs attack any nearby creatures indiscriminately.
 
Hoochiefs After Environmental Improvements in the Dim Forest:
Following improvements to the Dim Forest's biological environment, new cases of Hoochief infections from toxic spores have dropped significantly. Thanks to the intervention of antibodies developed by the Dim Forest exploration team, infections among Hoochiefs have gradually disappeared, ultimately dispelling the darkness that once shrouded the Dim Forest.

The Exiles are not a criminal organization with a unified leadership. Rather, the term refers to individuals who reject the control of local authorities and roam the wilds. They come from all walks of life and form a diverse, mixed group. While not inherently malicious, they have few qualms about committing illegal acts such as theft or robbery.
 
To survive in the harsh, unsheltered wilderness, they make use of scavenged materials and repurpose technology. Each Exile is typically armed with a Tacetite Weapon, obtained through illegal means, to defend against the threat of TDs or rival Exile gangs.
 
Jinzhou's stance toward the Exiles is primarily preventative, with security forces deployed in areas frequented by them. For those Exiles without significant offenses, the authorities generally adopt a more lenient approach and sometimes try to persuade them to submit under certain conditions. However, for Exiles who are recalcitrant and pose a security risk, the authorities are quick to eliminate them without hesitation.
 
Given the Exiles' long history, it is now difficult to trace when the first true Exile emerged.
 
There are numerous reasons why someone might choose to join the Exiles in the wilderness: a thief seeking to escape the Patrollers, a deserter too ashamed to face their comrades, or a Resonator who believes they can protect themselves but refuses to adhere to local laws. To become an Exile, one must first defeat another Exile—whether by taking their life, stealing their Ring, or seizing it by force, a symbol of severance from mainstream society. That is how an Exile earns recognition from their peers.

Surviving in the wilderness is a harsh and unforgiving challenge, which is why you should not expect an Exile to adhere to civilized norms. Most Exiles live by the law of the jungle, where strength and cunning are the only reliable assets. They train their bodies and hone their weapon skills in camps, learn to identify rare plants and minerals, and navigate secret paths through ridges and waterways that only they know. Some even develop techniques to avoid drawing the attention of the TDs.

These survival skills are regarded as treasures by various Exile factions, as valuable as life itself. But when the price is right, they don't mind offering their services to civilians, travelers, or merchants—acting as hitmen, searching for rare materials, or handling less-than-reputable jobs. Although trading with an Exile is not illegal in Jinzhou, it is also not protected by law. If an Exile sees you as easy prey, they may simply disregard any agreements, rob you clean, and leave you by the side of the road.

Only a rare few Exiles retain any sense of dignity or honor. While they reject the authorities, they consider themselves part of human society. These Exiles will fight against TDs when they can, defend their settlements, and sometimes even form unspoken pacts of non-aggression with other Exile factions.

Report No.: 94001 After extensive preparations, we finally crossed Desorock Highland and reached Norfall Valley within two weeks. However, due to the presence of the Groundwave Barrier, even with our specialized protective gear, it was impossible to deploy our full force into the valley at once. As a result, the Outriders were sent ahead to conduct reconnaissance and prepare for the moment anticipated by the General and foretold by the Sentinel. In the Battle Beneath the Crescent, the crescent moon of doom hung high in the sky... That battle is now in the past, yet upon returning to this valley, the echoes of tragic wails still linger in the air. It is impossible to tell if they are TD simulations or the "phantoms" of fallen warriors... Countless soldiers perished in unimaginable agony and desperation during that conflict, where allies and enemies were indistinguishable. I can hardly bring myself to remember those moments... Pushed by General Jiyan, Huaxu Academy developed the Retroact Rain antidote, meaning we were not completely defenseless. But when the Retroact Rain was enhanced by the Threnodian force, only those with Resonance powers could withstand its unrelenting strain on the mind. Ordinary soldiers were powerless to bear its crushing weight... Due to limited intelligence and reckless decisions, we paid a heavy price in the Battle Beneath the Crescent. General Jiyan led us through a narrow breach out of the Norfall Barrens, establishing Vanguard Base just outside Norfall Valley, where we have held our ground ever since. We cannot afford to let such a tragedy unfold again. General Jiyan has drawn the attention of most TDs outside Norfall Valley, buying us crucial time to conduct reconnaissance. The Groundwave Barrier disrupts all communication signals, so if anyone is separated from the main force, the positioning system won't be able to track them again. Getting lost here is as good as a death sentence. From this point on, we're on our own. Every step must be taken with the utmost caution. ... After a long journey spent covering our tracks, dodging the TDs, and bearing the pressure of the Groundwave Barrier, the team is utterly exhausted. But finally, we've made it to the cliff. From what we've seen along the way, transportation within Norfall Valley is severely restricted—far too narrow for large military machines, especially with the constant risk of falling rocks. If a conflict erupts here, the idea of ordinary people navigating heavy Tacetite machinery is practically impossible. This must be why General Jiyan shifted tactics, allowing only Resonators with Resonance Energy to join Vanguard Base. Looking toward the depths of the Norfall Barrens, we can see that the Ruins still hover in the distance. We set up the long-range recon device, revealing a swarm of highly agitated TDs moving restlessly amid eerie shrieks echoing through the air. That sound brings back memories of the monster in the Battle Beneath the Crescent.

We've been gathering intelligence on Ovathrax. In the Battle Beneath the Crescent, that creature took countless lives, and to our horror... we saw it deliberately mimic our swordplay and tactics. This ability resembles Ovathrax's recorded ability of "feeding on the frequencies of battle to fuel its own strength." But was that truly Ovathrax? According to the records we've compiled, the creature's frequency and stance align more closely with the Crownless. Most likely, it was just a vanguard sent by Ovathrax.

After we withdrew to the outskirts of Norfall Valley, it ceased its assault, suggesting its real purpose was to gather strength—fueling Ovathrax's evolution and buying time for its ultimate arrival. The Battle Beneath the Crescent may well have served as its feast.

...

After conducting reconnaissance on the Suspended Ruins, the team observed a faint purple light blinking in a distinct pattern. Has anyone else noticed this anomaly before? Could the Groundwave Barrier have obscured its presence? Is it some sort of distress signal? Could there be survivors still in the Norfall Barrens? Yet, the frequency of the blinking fills me with a sense of unease...

After discussing our options, the team decided to press forward and descend the Norfall Cliff in an attempt to get closer to the Suspended Ruins. But as we descended, that same unsettling feeling returned. We realized that the purple light seemed to be following us. The blinking frequency made me uneasy, reminding me of something blinking its eyes, as though it was watching us...

Archived Record in the City Hall:
The Outriders team had completed most of the reconnaissance of Norfall Valley. However, during their descent from the cliff, they encountered interference from an unknown frequency. This disruption resulted in an ambush by a large number of TDs. According to General Jiyan's report, he sensed the situation through the winds and issued coordination orders to the rear forces. He then breached the Groundwave Barrier and successfully extracted the team. Fortunately, there were no casualties among the team members, though several devices were lost in the process. However, the strain of breaching the Groundwave Barrier caused multiple organ damage in General Jiyan. During his recovery, he remained at Vanguard Base.

This is... a record of movie reviews from the Solaris Film Festival in the Somnoire?
Oh my gosh, people actually held a film festival in the Somnoire?
 
Review by [Pure Dream] Dorothy the Wonderous Adventurer; Rating: 9/10
 
Ugh, this is too much! The screenwriter is just... too much! I can't accept this ending! Why, why, why?! Jiu promised he'd give Yuehui a happy ending, but then he says, "I don't want to say goodbye, nor make promises with you." What does that even mean?! The final scene, with them reuniting on those big birds, was beautiful, yes... but why can't they just go back to how it was? Noooo! That sucked! I'm knocking off a point for this!

Review by [Wishes Under a Clear Sky] Miss Orange; Rating: 8/10

This is a film about love, and the scene that sticks with me the most is when Jiu and Yuehui finally reunite at that Lollo Logistics station, the place where they first met. Their dialogue there really nailed the essence of love. It's not just about the romance, but the real, everyday life that makes us feel whole. People are unlike the two legendary birds. Sure, Jiu will eventually meet someone else, or maybe try to force himself to forget, but some things will always remind him of her. It's just like that last scene when he's lost in thought at the Jinzhou Teahouse, staring at the painting on the wall.

Review by [Deepsea Solitude] White Dried Fish; Rating: 10/10
 
Although we can't fully understand human emotions, it doesn't stop us from savoring them. A solid 10! Yummy, meow.
 
Review by [Scales of Death] Aurelia; Rating: 8.3/10
 
This movie's editing? Top-notch. The pacing? Chef's kiss. During the slower parts, the handheld shots on Jinzhou's streets really nailed the vibe. That moment lives on in my head rent-free. The transitions and camera choices, especially when following the characters, were so on point. And that reverse shot at the Lollo Logistics station during the rain? Pure brilliance. It hinted at the unexpected twist without giving anything away.

Story-wise, it's a classic: the two leads meet, then part ways, with the plot coming full circle at the end. It's a little predictable and very tidy, but honestly, it works. It's sincere, and that's what makes it hit hard. I'm giving it an 8.3 because it's a true gem in today's world of cinema.

The first page of the New Branch Employee Handbook, distributed by KU-Tata. It provides an overview of the Black Shores ground level.
 
As the think tank for Lament prediction and world salvation, the Black Shores is also referred to as the "singularity for observing the Lament." Over the course of civilization, it has focused on studying the Lament and Waveworn Phenomena. Black Shores members travel globally to collect Reverberation samples from Lament zones, using the Tethys System to reverse-engineer them. Their goal is to replicate the premonitions and processes of the Lament in order to pinpoint its original source. By feeding a large volume of Reverberation specimens into the system, they aim to improve the accuracy of the Lament and Waveworn Phenomenon forecasts, reducing losses for their allies.

The Black Shores Archipelago is built on a massive piece of Tacetite, rich in high-dimensional Remnant Energy, which powers the endless computational cost of the Tethys System. Additionally, the vast energy field generated by the Tacetite's frequency forms a natural barrier that conceals the Black Shores within the seas. For those outside the organization, entry to the Black Shores is by invitation only, under the guidance of the Shorekeeper.

Jinzhou, the fortress city that guards the border of Huanglong, also stands as Huanglong's first border of entry for those arriving from overseas. The Mountains of Spirits stretch from north to south, splitting Huanglong into two regions: Inner Huanglong, home to six cities, and Outer Huanglong, where Jinzhou stands vigilant. These mountains form a natural barrier, with the gorges acting as the only gateway into Inner Huanglong, protected day and night by Jinzhou's Midnight Rangers.
 
The establishment of the first fortress in Outer Huanglong began with the emergence of the Norfall Barrens Tacet Field, where TD Outbreaks began to ravage the region. After enduring months of grueling combat, the army could no longer withstand the onslaught of the TD Outbreaks and was forced to retreat to the Gorges of Spirits, making their final stand. The warriors held their ground for days, fiercely battling as the defense lines were breached and reclaimed multiple times. During this time, the Waveworn Phenomenon across Huanglong appeared to be in an active phase, and it seemed as though the TDs were being led by a mysterious leader, aiming to converge in Inner Huanglong.

At the critical moment, reinforcements from the six cities were dispatched to the Gorges of Spirits, where the border warriors were still fighting with unwavering resolve. As the battle reached its peak, the appearance of the Crownless shattered the stalemate. Wherever the Crownless manifested, darkness enveloped the sky, and an oppressive atmosphere took hold, suffocating the warriors. Still, they held the line, willing to sacrifice themselves to buy time to destroy the entrance to the Gorges of Spirits and halt the TD Outbreak. They did so knowing it would trap most of them in Outer Huanglong with the TDs forever.
 
In that moment of life and death, a mighty Loong's roar emerged from the depths of the Gorges of Spirits, reverberating like thunder across the land. The roar burst forth from the Gorge, forcing back the TD army poised to flood in. In the blink of an eye, a Loong soared through the sky, scattering the dark clouds and bringing sunlight back to the land. Then, an otherworldly figure with golden eyes appeared, standing between the TDs and the warriors, confronting the Crownless in a fierce standoff. As the poem goes, "Armors gleam golden with Loong scales in the sun." As reinforcements from the six cities arrived, the united forces drove the TD Outbreaks and the Crownless back to the northern reaches of the Central Plains.
 
After this battle, Outer Huanglong was reborn from the ashes. The emergence of both the Threnodian and the holy creature signaled the need for a new city to rise and serve as Huanglong's border stronghold. Drawing inspiration from the "Jin" sound in "Guan Jin," meaning "the pass," and the form of Jin from the character symbolizing the roar of a Loong, this city was named Jinzhou.

Each area within the Black Shores Archipelago serves a specific function, including personnel management, issuing warnings, hosting international envoys, and providing living and preparation areas for Black Shores Consultants and Bloom Bearers.

Its true core, however, lies deep underground in Tethys' Deep—a highly classified zone off-limits to anyone outside the organization.

For years, the Black Shores has been collecting Reverberation data, recruiting skilled personnel, and liaising with other nations to advance efforts in analyzing the Lament.

As a global salvation organization, the Black Shores aims to minimize the impact of the Lament on civilization, help allies avoid threats, assist with reconstruction, and offer neutral advisory services during disasters. Notably, only the ground level is accessible to international envoys, where visitors are welcomed, daily affairs are managed, and information is exchanged.

Report on Lampylumen The Tiger's Maw Mine primarily produces Lampylumen along with other ore deposits, as well as a minor quantity of Tacetite ores. Following years of joint research by Huaxu Academy and the Ministry of Development, a unanimous conclusion has been reached regarding the formation of the Tiger's Maw. They found that tectonic shifts caused by the Waveworn Phenomenon altered the plate tectonics in Jinzhou, uplifting ore deposits formed tens of millions of years ago to the upper crust and introducing Lampylumen into the domain of human knowledge. The initial survey of the Lampylumen veins has led to the following conclusions: Form: Lampylumen typically has a cubic structure, often found as singular cubes or stacked formations, and its rectangular shape allows for easy extraction. It melts at high temperatures, making it easy to shape. Properties: Due to its unique formation, Lampylumen has an internal structure arranged like an electrical network, making it an ideal material for semiconductor sheets. Application: Lampylumen can be used in chips for Terminals and Resonance Beacons, as well as in the manufacturing of various high-precision components (further assessment required).

Report on Hypothermia Incident The newly surveyed mine, designated T36E8, has developed a freezing fog accompanied by an unusual buzzing sound that spreads with the mist. Until the source of the fog is identified, all survey operations in mine T36E8 have been suspended. Following the appearance of the freezing fog, mining machinery has been unable to reach operating temperatures or issue safety warnings. Multiple health monitors on-site have reported hypothermia warnings among workers. The Midnight Rangers have entered the mine to conduct an emergency rescue. Wounded miners have been transferred to the Medical Division of Huaxu Academy. In response, the Ministry of Development has deployed the Defense Division to secure and lock down the T36E8 site. Symptoms among the affected miners include delirium, hallucinations, and hypothermia. These conditions, along with abnormal vital signs, have not responded to standard medical treatments. The preliminary assessment points to a potential assault incident involving TDs.

A tourism guide penned by the Pioneer Association, featuring reports on the Hongzhen hot spring in Mt. Firmament.

[Tranquility’s Healing Touch] Spring's Taste

Spring's Taste is a centuries-old hot spring inn nestled in Hongzhen, set against the foothills beside a natural hot spring and known for its distinctive architectural style. After the slowed time flow on Mt. Firmament was lifted, the inn has finally opened to outside visitors. Here, snowflakes drift down as steam rises into the warm glow of lantern light, creating a serene atmosphere for guests soaking in the hot spring, with views of the undulating, snow-laden mountains in Mt. Firmament. This experience promises to dissolve all fatigue and stress! Many visitors leave Hongzhen with a lingering sense of awe and wonder, as though they've glimpsed a celestial realm—making Spring's Taste the top hot spring destination in all of Huanglong!
 
[Hot Spring Egg Challenge] Perfect Coddled Egg
 
As the oldest hot spring inn on Solaris-3, Spring's Taste offers food and lodging that reflect the authentic essence of Mt. Firmament, earning unanimous praise from its guests. The owner is a renowned foodie with a deep love for life and gourmet cuisine. Taking full advantage of the natural hot spring, he invented a unique method of "hot spring slow cooking," where food is sealed in jars and soaked in the hot spring to cook slowly.
 
Each year, Spring's Taste hosts a Hot Spring Egg Challenge, where participants compete to cook the perfect egg with a custard-like yolk. The winner is said to earn a year of free accommodations at the inn!

[Nature's Majestic Cascade] Snowy Stream
 
Mt. Firmament is home to many natural hot springs, and the scenic Snowy Stream is the source of Hongzhen's hot springs. A blooming tree's branches cradle the cascading waterfalls from the cliff, nourishing the entire hot spring system of Hongzhen.
 
This tree was planted by Hongzhen's first settlers when the town was first established. Over time, it has grown from a crack in the rock and now stands tall and proud. The waterfalls, constantly beating against the mountain rocks, have gradually polished the once-hard stones into smooth, rounded surfaces.
 
Later, the people of modern-day Hongzhen refined the landscape to replicate the legendary story of Snowy Stream from Mt. Firmament. Several centuries ago, a mysterious figure journeyed through the region when a heavy snowfall sealed off the mountain passes. Seeing the villagers' firewood supplies dwindling, the traveler used Resonance power to carve a passage through the mountains and divert the mountain stream to the village. In an instant, mist and melting ice flowed westward with the stream, creating a breathtaking sight as if ethereal immortals were gliding across the water's surface.

A page of the New Branch Employee Handbook, distributed by KU-Tata. It provides an overview of the Black Shores underground level.

The underground of the Black Shores is where its data space intersects with reality, also known as Tethys' Deep.

In other words, the underground space of the Black Shores is the Tethys System itself. Space Anchors, stabilizing devices positioned throughout the surface and underground levels, act as firewalls to maintain the balance between the data zone and reality, ensuring they do not interfere with each other.

If the Space Anchors malfunction, the data zone within the Tethys System can "invade" reality, triggering anomalies that, according to the records, include but are not limited to:

Regional overlap between the digital space and the physical world, an increased likelihood of Consultants and Bloom Bearers developing spatial perception disorders, and simulated objects from the Sand Table escaping into reality.

The Tethys System consists of two key components: the Data Torrent and the Stellar Matrix, a supercomputational Sand Table that imitates the celestial bodies.

Using the data of the Lament to observe and analyze its mechanisms, and thereby forewarn future occurrences of the Lament, are the duties of the "stars."

However, this is just the beginning of the application and exploration of the Tethys System. The Black Shores Consultants are actively working to unlock its full potential.
 
They say that the one with the highest clearance within the Black Shores was able to harness the Stellar Matrix's full computational capacity to simulate the future of civilization. However, this attempt led to the system's resources being drained to the point of near-total shutdown.

While the Order often lauds water for its tranquility, gentleness, birthing of life, and enriching nature, it can also symbolize instability. Ragunna faces constant threats from tides and floods. Everything in Ragunna arises from the sea, yet everything ultimately returns to it.

Surrounded by the sea, the people of Ragunna live in harmony with the water. Whether driven by love or fear, the Ragunnesi hold a deep reverence for it. In a sense, this also reflects their anxiety and fear of the Final Tide, as foretold by the Sentinel.

They hold various rituals to pray to the Sentinel, hoping that the Sentinel will guide them through the tides of this life and ultimately lead them through the Final Tide.

Scholars of the Order have also drawn inspiration from myths surrounding the Sentinel Imperator, developing an entire set of theories about water.

[Theory I: The Origin of the World is Water]
Water is universally present in everything and encompasses all things, representing infinity. It is an object of infinite nature. Everything originates from water, including the creation of the world itself.

[Theory II: Water is Fluid, Like the Constant Movement of the Tide]
In its movement, water is divided into the contrasting sides of cold and hot, dry and wet, forming the world. The movement of water is the tide. Everything is born in the tide and will eventually end in the Final Tide. However, this end does not signify obliteration. Just as everything originates from water, the end is merely a return to the embrace of water. This movement creates a cycle, ultimately reuniting everything in the sea. From this reunion, humans will again be separated, only to be reborn like spring shoots, in an infinite cycle.

[Theory III: Water is Reflective]
The Ragunnesi believe that water reflects everything without discrimination, allowing humans to see another version of themselves within it.

Water mirrors the appearance of the Ragunnesi, and the Ragunnesi, in turn, see their reflections in the water. If the world is like an ocean, then the frequencies of humans and the world influence and shape one another. The wondrous water has been imbued with the human spirit, symbolizing the cycle of life and death. If water represents the subconscious, it also serves as a harbor for fantasies and desires.

This is why research into the Remnant domain is also prevalent within the Order.

The Seminary of the Forgotten in Rinascita was once flooded by Nimbus Sanctum, which later proved to be a manifestation of Remnant Energy, recording the emotions and memories of humans without distinction, and then reflecting them in reality.

With the old site of the Seminary still present, Nimbus Sanctum holds a special allure for Acolytes of the Order, who visit to pray or salvage ancient texts.
Some scholars believe the Remnant Cloud is a higher-dimensional form of water, while others speculate that another world exists beneath Nimbus Sanctum.

[Theory IV: Water is All-Encompassing]
This all-encompassing nature is why Ragunna, under the guidance of the Order, is a city that welcomes exiles from all walks of life and grants them equal rights. The Carnevale is the epitome of this inclusiveness. Ragunnesi from various isles unite to honor their hometowns and families lost in the Lament. Dressed in their traditional clothing and wearing masks symbolizing ancestors and totems, they perform a variety of dramas. The diversity and inclusiveness lie at the core of the performances during the Carnevale.

[Theory V: Unity]
Taking inspiration from the all-encompassing nature of water, Primus Fenrico, upon assuming power, developed the doctrine of Unity and enshrined it in the Codex.

For the exiled people of Rinascita, formed after the Lament, religion is not merely a practice in the Order but a collection of science, philosophy, politics, individual identity, and the hope for salvation. The civilization of Rinascita is anchored around faith, meaning religion is not just a personal pursuit but a universal truth that explains the world and defines one's place within it.

Any heretical theory that undermines or challenges this faith is seen as a dagger aimed at the heart of truth itself. Such ideas threaten the existence of those around them and risk tearing apart the fabric of society, bringing calamity and destruction to this city by the sea.

The Primus believes that whenever the ideology of Division reaches its zenith, the calamity of the Dark Tide will descend from above, endangering the very existence of Rinascita. For this reason, even the Carnevale, which embodies the spirit of inclusiveness, must be overseen by the Order.

I once joked to a friend that if, one day, you find yourself wanted across all of Solaris-3 for illegal actions like short selling or trading in debts, then, based on my experience, apart from digging your own grave, your best bet would be to hide in Averardo Vault in Rinascita. As long as you can prove your worth, the Montelli family will keep you safe—even if it means turning a blind eye. They'll go so far as to pay your bail out of their own pockets and assemble a professional international legal team for you, with only one condition: that you build strong business ties with them. Trust me on this, I deal a lot with the Montellis. They value the so-called "spirit of the contract" more than most businessmen. Back when I was younger, I couldn't stand those brash islanders. They didn't play by the rules, were full of energy, and always spoke their minds. They were nothing like the Rinascitan people I knew, who were all about dance and performance. But over time, I came to recognize a trait in them that others lacked. They always price everything upfront. The Montellis are by far the easiest businessmen to understand because their world operates on just one principle: the contract. And the only thing driving that principle? Profit. —Excerpt from How to Get Unlimited Shell Credits

A report from the Ministry of Development, archived in the City Hall. Its filing date suggests that it was submitted decades ago.
 
Infrastructure Division of the Ministry of Development in Jinzhou of Huanglong:
 
The Jinzhou Expansion Project Phase II has completed its initial preparation work. We are now submitting the land use application for construction approval. Below is the relevant information regarding the project:
 
I. Construction Undertaker Overview:
 
The Land Development Team of the Infrastructure Division is a construction project undertaker affiliated with Jinzhou's Ministry of Development, responsible for managing construction efforts in the Jinzhou region. Initially, the team consisted of 60 employees. Following the recruitment and transfers during the post-war period, the team has now grown to 400 ad-hoc members. This includes 31 individuals from the original staff, 190 transfers from Huaxu Academy, the Midnight Rangers, and the Defense Division of the Ministry of Development, 120 volunteers from Jinzhou, 50 transfers from other regions, and 9 individuals of unknown origin.

As long as projected earnings outweigh the risks, the Montellis will go to any lengths to fulfill the contract. They never turn down a deal that lands on their doorstep and always deliver once the client has paid. Their team possesses a unique, almost magnetic force, uniting individuals driven by ambition and the promise of fame. But don't expect to hear talk of ethics or loyalty—profit is the only metric that matters. It's hard to wrap your head around, isn't it? A family that has its hands in Echo technology, global trade, banking, private arms, and once even currency manipulation, yet they don't rely on bloodlines to sustain the empire. Decades have passed, and the fortune stashed in Averardo Vault must be beyond imagination. To protect it, they've even imported specialized tech and upgraded their Echoes into formidable war machines. Trust me, gentlemen—no matter how confident you are in your abilities, never, ever even entertain the thought of going after that vault. —Excerpt from How to Get Unlimited Shells

In my observation, up until six or seven years ago, most people sent to the Fool's Sails never really believed they'd end up there.

Back then, Acolytes still tried to persuade those who had gone astray, reminding them they had a choice and could still change their ways. If only they knew their fate, they would surely alter it.

I believe that at the time, most Acolytes genuinely preached with compassion, even though they couldn't foresee the consequences.

After all, everything that needs to be foreseen is already laid out in the oracle of the Primus, isn't it?

"Wait not to correct mistakes after they are made. Save the misguided before they act foolishly."

Without the revelation of the Enlightened One, this idea is undoubtedly a paradox: humans cannot decide the outcome before the cause—just as it is impossible for a child to be born before the mother. But this, in fact, is the very greatness of the Primus. This is the grace granted by our Sentinel!

I am simply filled with awe:

O how great you are, Fenrico, the Enlightened One! O how great Thou are, Sentinel Imperator!

As an employee at the Ragunna branch of the Pioneer Association, I rarely bring up my hometown with colleagues.

I come from a small town called Egla, which fits every definition of a "small town"—simple, a bit behind the times, and quiet, at least during daylight hours. Through my business travels worldwide, I've seen many such towns. Most eventually merge into larger, fortified cities for protection from TDs or the Lament. Few people realize, however, that Egla's history as a settlement is nearly as ancient as Ragunna's, and it had stubbornly kept much of its original character.

Within the Order, there's a well-known piece of advice: never anger the elders of Egla.

Visitors to Egla might encounter a few lively elders who seem like humble figures, be it a local mayor or an innkeeper. But behind these modest roles, many were once people of influence, even retired Acolytes or Priests of the Order who served alongside the Primus, interpreted the oracles, or shaped doctrines. When Ragunna was still a city on the rise, these elders—or their forebears—stood on the front lines, helping lay its very foundations. After long, distinguished careers, they returned to Egla, choosing to spend their later years in the place where it all began.

What is it, exactly, that keeps people returning to Egla Town?
 
Honestly, I can't quite understand the mindset of that generation.
 
The last time I left my hometown, I saw a group of elders gathered in front of an abandoned house, almost as if they were holding a vigil.
 
They stood there for a long time in silence before one of them spoke, reflecting on the past:
 
"Old friend, time doesn't turn back. You can't live forever in what might have been. You need to understand that the present isn't necessarily worse than the past. It might even be better... We couldn't save that child in the end. But we should be grateful for the majority we did save."

This is a transcript of an interview that occurred in the Montelli family.

- Good day. I've been assigned as your consultant for this case. You can refer to me as No. 35.

- No. 35? Don't you have an actual name?

- I beg your understanding, sir. Those of us in this line of work prefer to keep our dealings strictly professional, with no entanglement beyond the task at hand.

- Alright, then. What's your plan regarding this employee's contract?

- Termination.

- And...? No emotional support, no severance, no kind words to soften the blow?

- No. Just termination.

- What? Then why would the Montellis need you for this? I could handle it myself, and probably better.

- Are you sure, sir? Are you prepared to look this young woman in the eye—a girl who's worked tirelessly for this family, despite being separated from her own mother—and tell her, without a hint of empathy, "I'm sorry, but you haven't brought sufficient value to the family. We have to let you go." If you're certain you can do that, then be my guest.

- I... I can certainly do that. Besides, there's no need to be so harsh, is there?

- If you're not harsh enough, sir, you may very well be the next to face dismissal. Be too lenient, and you risk failing to generate value for the family and wasting extra compensation. Even if you manage the dismissal, the staff may start seeing you as cold-hearted. The Montellis are a big family, aren't they? Who would do that to their own family?

For several days, we tracked a "mechanical reindeer herd" across the frostlands. Our path led us through ravines flanked by cubic cliffs and rows of monoliths, culminating in the discovery of a vast "underground haven" beneath the permafrost. There, we encountered an ancient human tribe: the Roya.
 
Physiologically, the Roya differ little from us. The distinctions lie mostly in the subtle traits they've developed to survive the extreme cold. Within this colossal subterranean cavern, an astonishing energy source, known to the Roya as "Baldur's Heart," pulses without end, providing the light and warmth needed to sustain life in this underground region. Sustained by this "sunlight," the Roya have built a new home under its rays. Over countless generations, they have studied the rhythms of Baldur's Heart, devising their own system of timekeeping to mark the cycle of day, night, seasons, and years, living in quiet synchrony with the world above.
 
According to Royan mythology, certain "mechanical creatures" that roam the frostlands—which they call Soliskin, and we classify as the Exoswarm—are considered countless sparks of Baldur's own consciousness. In gratitude for the light Baldur bestowed, the Roya have taken up a sacred, generational duty: to guide lost Soliskin back to this sanctuary and live alongside them. After millennia bathed in the Reactor Drive's radiance, the Roya of today can now walk the frostlands wearing little more than Lahai-Roi's light garments.
 
We once hailed Lahai-Roi as one of the greatest scientific discoveries of the century, yet we have refrained from making it public. The Pioneer Association's leadership agrees that releasing this "earthshaking revelation" may spark uncontrollable consequences. The Roya, isolated for generations, might develop a deep curiosity for the outside world, while modern civilization, in turn, may cast its own judgment upon this ancient one. 
 
Would this lead to communication and coexistence, or to intrusion and exploitation? No one can guarantee the outcome. Thus, the Pioneer Association must handle this research report with the utmost caution.

Time, it seems, is a luxury we can no longer afford.
 
According to our personnel in Lahai-Roi, several outside institutions, having obtained leaked intelligence, have already dispatched their own investigative teams. Their goal is to lay claim to the region's discoveries before the world can take notice.
 
Among them are earnest researchers, driven by curiosity and respect. But there are also "poachers" cloaked in the guise of "civilization." These intruders plunder Lahai-Roi's natural wealth at will and treat the Roya as a backward tribe. They offer the Roya trinkets common in the outside world or even obsolete technologies, attempting to purchase trust and gratitude at a paltry cost. Not once have they regarded the Roya by the ethical standards they claim to uphold.
 
Simultaneously, some within the Roya tribe itself grow restless. Those who have forgotten or even scorn their ancestral mission. Now, driven by rebellion against tradition or by a fervent longing for the outside world, they seek to "leave the frostlands" through drastic means. They barter away tribal knowledge, resources, even technology... And for this betrayal, they have been cast out, becoming "Outcasts," wandering beyond the tribe's protection.
 
The "Pandora's Box beneath the frostlands" has been opened. Thus, the Pioneer Association signatories have resolved to selectively and strategically disclose portions of our scientific findings to the global public.
 
Just as the leader of the Black Shores once remarked, this is a negotiation laid bare before all nations. Once key information about Lahai-Roi is public, every state will be compelled to approach the same table and, together with the Roya, determine the future of Lahai-Roi itself.

To uphold their shared commitment to peace and cooperation, the signatories of the Pioneer Association met. After lengthy talks, their heads of state decided to form a new intergovernmental organization named the "Polar Collective" (Editor's note: the predecessor to the Spacetrek Collective).
 
Just as the conference was ending, a Roya elder, one of their revered Solsworn, appeared before the assembly.
 
Speculation and whispers about his intentions rippled through the hall. Most delegates regarded him with the subtle arrogance of a "civilized world" appraising a representative of an ancient tribe. Unfazed, the Solsworn began to draw a series of intricate, cryptic patterns, murmuring to himself as he worked. At first, many dismissed them as nothing more than curses or meaningless doodles. But as the patterns took shape, the truth emerged—they were formulae.
 
The symbols he used were from a numbering system entirely alien to our own, but once "converted" into modern notation, the structures they described matched some of our most advanced equations. The very kind of mathematics we believe can change the world. In that moment, the assembly understood the significance of the Solsworn's act. It demonstrated that the Roya possessed knowledge and mathematical mastery on par with our own, and more importantly, that they were willing to share this ancient wisdom with the Polar Collective.
 
In that moment, mathematics became the only language in the room. With a few simple points and lines drawn in an instant, the Solsworn completed an astronomical measurement of the polar axis. Its precision matched, perhaps even surpassed, that of our finest contemporary instruments. Awe gradually gave way to silence. There was no longer any doubt: the Roya's accomplishments had not only reached but now challenged the intellectual dominion claimed by the so-called civilized world.
 
The silence did not last. The Solsworn then presented a second set of equations. They described the presence of the Waveworn Phenomenon within Lahai-Roi, showing that its activity had been steadily increasing over time. Yet, at the conclusion of this formulation, the Solsworn offered no solution.
 
Meanwhile, the arrival of the Black Shores only deepened the unease. Observations from the Tethys System had long indicated traces of a Threnodian in Lahai-Roi, but its frequency shared no commonality with any known Threnodian signature on Solaris. In other words, it did not originate from Solaris, nor from any recognizable civilization.
 
As scholars debated the equations, a formless dread seeped through the assembly. Were they misinterpreting the data? Or was the formulation itself incomplete? Perhaps the Solsworn was not deliberately withholding the final answer. Perhaps the answer itself was  "unknowable." 

This implied that, for the first time, humanity did not know, and was incapable of uncovering, the true nature of the "concept" it faced.
 
How does one fight an unknowable enemy? If the "concept" of this Threnodian cannot be known, then its form and capabilities remain equally opaque. In other words, every weapon humanity has devised could be rendered useless.
 
All would collapse into a single, all-consuming unknown.

[Wufang Liondance: A Fusion of Music and Movement] Huanglong Taiping Musical
 
The Huanglong Taiping Musical, also known as the liondance in Jinzhou, began as a battle dance commemorating the victories of Huanglong's army. At the heart of the performance is the lion, representing a triumphant return, accompanied by powerful drumbeats, lively music, and dynamic movements. These elements energize the dancers while uplifting the audience's morale.
 
Originally a battle dance, the liondance gradually evolved into a symbol of courage and a ritual for invoking peace—driving away bad omens while welcoming good fortune.
 
As the saying goes, the Wufang Lion Dance illustrates the lion's tameness and playfulness within the Seven Stars. To follow the Five Directions, one must understand the Seven Stars, and vice versa.
 
The liondancers, full of energy, change their steps to convey emotions from joy to sadness, shifting from rage to drunkenness. The drum beats mirror these transitions, moving from gentle to thunderous. The dancers follow the rhythm to portray the lion's various moods and movements—sometimes startled, sometimes joyful, sometimes running, sometimes pausing. When the lion is surprised, the drumming halts; when it looks around, the beats soften like a drizzle. When the lion is spirited, the drumming intensifies; and when the lion roars, the beats become thunderous.

The Roya's understanding of the phenomena within Lahai-Roi and the data they possess far surpasses that of any outside representative. If the world is to delve deeper into Lahai-Roi and find a solution, it must rely on the Roya as its "guide." Yet even with their vast knowledge, the Roya's current technological capabilities are insufficient to withstand the calamities born of the Threnodian. This, perhaps, is why the Solsworn appeared at the conference: in the face of Lahai-Roi's looming Threnodian crisis, the Roya had long harbored a willingness to cooperate with the outside world. They were simply waiting for the right moment, the moment they call the beginning of the "Twilight Epoch."

For the Roya, exposing themselves to the outside world may well be a gamble. But they believe that once this unfamiliar Threnodian awakens, the scale of its destruction will engulf all of Solaris... And for this, they have already steeled themselves.
 
Thus, each nation declared its stance: the Polar Collective would formally establish an alliance with the Roya and embark on joint expeditions into Lahai-Roi. At the same time, all activities carried out by the Collective must rest upon the foundation of peaceful agreements, causing no harm or disruption to Royan society.
 
The conference ended in harmony, yet no one left at ease. We had arrived driven by curiosity for Lahai-Roi's unknowns, only to depart with nothing but fear of that very unknown.
 
As the last New Federation scholar to leave remarked: "This fear... it's hard to name, but it's the oldest and strongest within us. And for humanity, that fear has always been the fear of the unknown."

...
 
The Roya once walked the surface, on ancient plains where the Glommoths and Glommothas thundered in their thousands. In the subarctic fjords, their ancestors lived as nomads, and even now, the shepherd's instinct still flows in their blood.

In Memory of Those Who Never Returned

Fellow citizens. Colleagues of the Spacetrek Collective. Faculty and students of Startorch Academy. And all of you still holding your posts in Lahai-Roi.

Today, we stand once more beneath the light of Helios.

The last time we gathered here, we celebrated the New Solar Ceremony. We had just ignited an artificial sun in Lahai-Roi's sky. We cheered for the future.

We didn't know that months later, we would endure the largest Void Storm on record. We would activate "Duskveil," our final contingency. And we would face the Threnodian, Aleph-One, head-on.

But we have driven the Threnodian back. We have sealed the Stridergate. We have crossed the Twilight Epoch, the very period of time Royan mythology said would end everything.

Yes. We have triumphed.

This victory is unprecedented. The known over the unknown. Humanity over the Threnodian.

But as the head of the Spacetrek Collective, it is my duty to tell you what this victory cost.

In the past months, Lahai-Roi has recorded nearly one hundred Void Storms. Five exceeded the highest alert level. Over thirty of our monitoring stations, research facilities, and defense nodes have been destroyed. In our search for the runes, we lost countless Mechascouts. Seventeen of our best operators suffered Voidmatter contamination. Most of them will never return to Lahai-Roi.

And most critically, we lost the cornerstone of the Spacetrek Collective itself. The Exostrider—the one who carved out Lahai-Roi's future.

And yet, this is the greatest victory we have ever achieved in our long war against the Voidborne Threnodian.

This frontier was built by the people of Solaris. Countless pioneers have been lost to the Void Storms. Their Cassettes still sit in the deepest vaults of our archives.

Roald, Koki, Mingxia, Beverly, Bajcetic—many of you have heard these names. They were the first explorers. The first researchers to come from every corner of Solaris to these frozen lands. And they were the first to try to conquer the void through their recordings, helping us learn the truth about Void Storms.

And before them, there were so many more whose Cassettes could not be recovered. They remain forever lost to the Void Storms.

Today, I stand here to recount these "costs." Not to dwell on suffering, but to remind you, and myself, that this very moment we are living through, and every tomorrow to come, is a chain of miracles built on the accumulation of all that came before.

I still remember my first speech after taking office here. It was at the memorial for the Roald expedition team.

Since then, I have witnessed the disappearance of many fine explorers.

But they were never just cold, lifeless names on a list. The traces they left behind still guide us forward.

Together with the Roya, lost in darkness since ages past, they endured. They resisted dissolution in eternal darkness.

The Roya. The people of Rinascita. The people of Huanglong... People from every corner of Solaris, even in the deepest darkness of the void, they resisted dissolution. They kept moving forward. They kept exploring.
...
...
...

As for what came after, I believe everyone here already knows. We are still standing here. Even when nothingness tried to consume all of Lahai-Roi, we are still standing here.

Yes. We have lost so much.

But right now, we are still standing. And we will keep moving forward.

Aleph-One tried to make us believe that everything eventually returns to nothing. But it was wrong. That signal, sent by a probe Solaris explorers launched years ago, was not white noise. Not cosmic background radiation. 

It was the voice of the beginning. The afterglow of the universe's birth. And we can still hear it, across billions of years.

So remember this: everything that has ever existed always leaves a trace.

The Spacetrek Collective will not stop. One day, we will break through the Etheric Sea. We will venture into a wider world.

And as the Exostrider once said:

May we meet again in the boundless sea of stars!

Twistscales

Listen. A low whistle accompanied by the sound of friction approaches from afar. That sphere, draped in hardened scales, bounds and weaves between steep cliff faces.
This is the Twistscales, one of the most peculiar creatures inhabiting these wilds.
Each time the morning mist disperses, the Twistscales is driven by an ancient and powerful instinct—to collect.
Within the interior of its heavy scales lies an extraordinarily keen nervous system. In its rolling and crawling, these hidden senses precisely capture the size of surrounding minerals, the position of fruits and branches upon the ground. Once it locks onto a target, powerful musculature draws the scales together, gripping these gifts of nature firmly in place. The tireless Twistscales rolls about restlessly until nightfall, as if intent on curling away the entire mountainside.
Yet in the harsh wilderness, greed often exacts a heavy price.
As the "spoils" wedged between its scales accumulate, the Twistscales can no longer maintain its compact, nimble spherical form. To bear this weight, it must unfurl its limbs. At this moment, the once swift cliff-runner can only trudge like an aged tortoise through the mud, each step laborious and unsteady, stopping frequently, breathing heavily.
But the wilds are fraught with danger. Predators may lurk in unseen corners, and once a threat is perceived, it curls into a ball at once. With a sharp clattering of collision, its scales snap shut in fright, and the treasures nestled between the seams slip free. The fruits of a day's labor scatter across the ground.
Typically, the Twistscales remains curled for about ten minutes, then begins to roll slowly until it confirms no threat lingers nearby, only then relaxing its body. After resting a moment, it coils into a ball once more and begins collecting the "spoils" scattered about.
Should this occur as the sun descends into the western sky, they return to the safe burrow constructed from liuheyinghua stone, wenhuabi jade, and tree branches. Only there does the Twistscales flip onto its belly and spend the night in its most comfortable posture.

The Golden Bell Beyond the Gate is a narrative performance piece arranged based on historical facts, recounting the evolution of Huanglong's Jinzhou region.
The author discovered that many historical elements within this performance can be used as reference material for comparative study regarding the Land of Xuanfang's history, and thus wrote this piece to cross-reference the historical facts in the performance with records from other documents for textual analysis to a certain degree.
...
The performance refers to Jinzhou as "the foremost fortress beyond Outer Huanglong," a gateway to the six cities, and the strategic point of Huanglong.
In fact, this assessment's formation is intimately connected to the Land of Xuanfang.
Before Jinzhou was established, the eastern coastal regions contained only scattered settlements (the precursors to Qichi Village and Taoyuan Vale). Post Lament, these regions gradually fell into decline, with only a small Huanglong garrison stationed there, which is what became known to people at the time as "Outer Huanglong." It was only after Huanglong, with the Land of Xuanfang as its center point, gradually recovered the lost eastern territories that Jinzhou emerged later, along with the Jinmen Pass from "The Golden Bell Beyond the Gate."
Today, Jinzhou lies outward, serving as the first overland port for external seas entering Huanglong, while the Land of Xuanfang lies inward, a vital waypoint on the path into Mengzhou. Together they form Huanglong's eastern bulwark, standing guard at the gate for the one capital and six cities.

As written in "The Golden Bell Beyond the Gate," the Battle of Gorges of Spirits is given particular emphasis, a campaign part of the "Fortress and Gorges War." The "Fortress" refers to Yuan Fortress, a place whose origins trace back to before Jinzhou's establishment.
Before the founding of Jinzhou, it was a region in ruins awaiting to be rebuilt, with nothing but several Huanglong border garrisons stationed there, re-surveying the Jinzhou territories post Lament, and a response force against small-scale TD Outbreaks.
Although Mt. Firmament in the southeastern corner also showed signs of Waveworn Phenomenon, Jué’s descent preserved the people of Hongzhen from the flow of time.
However, Jué was already gravely wounded upon Their arrival and began experiencing frequency overflow. It was then that Norfall Barrens saw a TD Outbreak emerge, targeted at Hongzhen... As beings that feed on frequency, the Sentinel's frequency served as a magnificent feast.
To protect the newborn flame of civilization from being extinguished and to prevent the Tacet Discords of Norfall Barrens from spreading to other cities of Huanglong, Mengzhou, being the nearest city, made the choice to construct a Mechanical citadel at one of its passes to serve as a blockade, and that pass is Xuanfang.
During this time, Mengzhou's Zhuojun Atelier dispatched large numbers of personnel to support the Ministry of Development, working together to complete the Mechanical fortress of Yuan, which delayed the TD Outbreak's invasion.
This mechanically constructed city, Yuan Fortress, built by human hands, became the predecessor to the Xuanfang Hold that would later hang suspended among the peaks and mists. The aforementioned "Fortress and Gorges War," which erupted at the Gorges of Spirits and Yuan Fortress, led to the completion of Xuanfang Hold, granting the Land of Xuanfang and Jinzhou a completely different future.

Ladies and gentlemen, today we shan’t speak of the Sentinel's tales, but rather recount a strange and wondrous story from the Land of Xuanfang a hundred years past!
Our tale begins in those bygone days. In the Land of Xuanfang, upon Western Fang Peaks, there dwelt a household of the Bi family, and their only son bore the single name "Zhong." From the moment Bi Zhong drew his first breath, he was unlike any other child of his age—while others chased scale-tailed beasts and teased Opus Otters, chattering and clamoring through the days, he remained quiet and reserved. Day in and day out, he loved only to crouch by the stone walls and dismantle wooden locks.
The days go past, and in twenty winters, our Bi Zhong had grown into a man sturdy as an iron tower. Eight feet tall, broad-shouldered, and sturdy as a rock. The man was blessed with great stature and a robust physique, matched with a stern face, and in his daily life, he seldom smiled or spoke carelessly. After his elderly mother passed away, there was scarcely a close confidant to whom he could speak his innermost thoughts. Yet to mistake him for a mere brute would be a grave mistake indeed!
Bi Zhong possessed extraordinary talent in the craft of ingenious Mechanisms. An Artisan would spend half a month studying blueprints, yet he could discern the flaws in load-bearing and joinery at a single glance. However intricate the Mechanism arrays and reconstructions, he could fashion them with ease. Moreover, his resolve was steadfast and his conviction profound, unmatched across the Western Peaks. Once he had drawn his designs, he believed them infallible and would face any obstacle head-on without hesitation.
Do you know, my fellow listeners? That the magnificent "Skyworks" which now stands towering between the Western Peaks is intimately connected to this very Bi Zhong!
Now, in those days upon the Western Peask, the load-bearing pivot of the "Segmented Corridor," the entrance to the Skyworks, suddenly tilted, and bricks and stones rained down like a deluge, teetering on the brink of collapse! Should it fall, countless mighty timbers, jade stones, and metals would come tumbling down the mountainside, bearing down upon the villages at the foot of the peak, sending the people into endless cries and fleeing in panic!
In this critical moment hanging by a thread, what fate awaited the people of the Western Peaks? And what could Bi Zhong accomplish in such dire straits? Find out in the next installment!

Previously, we spoke of how the Segmented Corridor teetered on the brink of collapse, and the looming great calamity! People scattered and fled in all directions, yet one man alone stood against the tide, shouldering a hammer and cradling timber, his steps heavy and resolute, charging straight toward that swaying load-bearing pivot! The man, none other than Bi Zhong!
Upon reaching the load-bearing pivot, he saw through its structural capability at a glance. He knew well that preserving the bearing was beyond reach. He could only buy time, granting the people precious moments to evacuate. Bi Zhong had to push the misaligned main shaft back into place by force, then support it with large timbers. Yet how immense was that main shaft, and now, through heat caused by friction, it glowed like burning coals!
Bi Zhong did not yield a single step. He clenched his teeth, the veins in his arms bulging like coiled serpents, each swing of his hammer striking with precision at the misaligned critical points of the load-bearing pivot. Amid the spray of sparks, rubble and broken bricks fell around him, striking his head, shoulders, and body. He remained as silent as ever, unmoved like a mountain.
Through such extraordinary resolve and confidence in his understanding of structure, he continued this for a full hour, pushing the main shaft back into place, then wedging the great timbers he had brought to seal the gap. A makeshift measure bought three hours in time!
Those precious three hours granted the people of the Western Peaks a chance to escape. Yet when the disaster had passed, and the people returned, excavating through the ruins, they found only scattered metal fragments, with Bi Zhong nowhere to be found.
Thereafter, the people of the Western Peaks, in gratitude for his benevolence, honored him with the title the "Son of Unyielding Virtue." A lone "Son" that walks among us, "Unyielding" in the face of peril, and of "Virtue" in sacrificing himself for the masses.
Some spoke in whispers that Bi Zhong did not perish. He emerged from the ruins and encountered a group of hermit masters. They recognized the righteousness of his deeds and treasured his craft, and this solitary figure at last found kindred spirits.
Yet time turned the seas to mulberry fields, and this tale is now a hundred years old. To this day, the truth of the legend of the "Son of Unyielding Virtue." And his whereabouts, no one knows.

...
That night, the gathering at Xianling Village was a splendid one, and I was fortunate to hear an ancient melody of the "Xuanling" sung upon the stage.
It was merely a series of lyrics, absent of any imagery, yet it left an indelible impression upon me.

I heard the performers upon the stage intone:

"On a desolate night of stone, dark clouds arise,
Twin moons share the sky, illuminating tattered banners.
Before Clouded Cliffs, the wind weeps as it blows,
Yuan Fortress's lanterns light the armored steel.
Xuanling flutters gracefully across the long embankment,
Thousand gates and myriad households all depart.
Who ventures forth upon the road to Mengzhou,
Who remains behind, refusing to abandon…"

I seemed to witness that night a hundred years past, soldiers standing resolute before the Fortress, common folk departing their homeland with reluctance, mothers cradling infants in their arms, fathers gripping their sons' hands.
Some among them perhaps left their native soil and never returned to the Land of Xuanfang in their lifetimes, while others perhaps forewent evacuation, leaving their blood and flesh upon this land that had nurtured them…

…
As the drumbeat grew louder, the chorus upon the stage finally reached its crescendo:
"A thousand towers crumble to the earth, forming into deep chasms,
A hundred bridges snap asunder, transformed into a heavenly rift.
Xuanfang's rain of fire obscures the long moon,
Ten thousand souls' cries of anguish shake the desolate wilderness."

But suddenly, the voices of all fell silent.
In the next moment, a woman's clear solo voice rose—
"Yuan Fortress' lofty framework left incomplete.
The entire city's Mechanisms turn to dust.
Xuanling once beheld,
Children chasing lanterns,
Elders listen to the dusk.
Yesterday's thousand households warm,
Tonight ten thousand bones grow cold."
Her gentle humming faded, like a silent flash of lightning—the air around the ears grew still, yet the heart was shaken.
At last, the chorus gradually rose once more, offering a prolonged and lingering coda to that night:
"Xuanling falls, the abyss is born.
Countless Tacet Discords all fade into darkness.
One city's loyal bones buried in endless night,
Half a moon shines alone upon an empty court."
…
Postscript at the end of the text:
When this essay was completed, I had just returned to Mengzhou from Xianling Village. Yet now, that journey to Xianling Village was already more than a decade past.
To this day, I still remember the village elders telling me when the gathering ended that night. If you hear sparrow calls in the deep of night, it is not the wind, but the Xuanling sparrows gazing back upon this land from beneath the abyss.

Opus Otters

Each day, when the lingering glow of sunset paints the riverbank of Eastern Xuan Peaks in shades of gold, the people of Xuanfang dwelling in these mountains share an unspoken accord: they cease their labors, and across the tranquil waters, they await that gentle tribe on the far shore to finish their foraging and begin the day's final clamor.
Long before the ancestors of the Land of Xuanfang learned to fell wood and craft stringed instruments, these waters already possessed their own natural musicians—Opus Otters.
Their mellow, rounded bodies are covered in dense fur, which helps the Opus Otters maintain warmth in the frigid waters. Yet their most peculiar adaptation is the lustrous, smooth Opus Stone embedded in their belly. The very poem that every child of the Land of Xuanfang commits to memory springs from this marvel.
"Water harbors Otters, cradling stones in song, their voices bright and clear, echoing through the shadowed mountains."
After sating themselves, the Opus Otters recline contentedly on the riverbank, their plump yet nimble forepaws grasping pebbles from the water's edge or hard shells, which they strike rhythmically against the Opus Stone on their belly. The crisp sounds of impact, intertwined with the piercing calls from deep within their throats, weave together into a natural, refined melody within the twilight valley.
This is not merely the otter colony's post-meal leisure and the social ritual of transmitting breeding signals, but has also become a healing solace in the hearts of the Xuanfang folk. Workers who have toiled the day through often sit upon the ground to listen quietly; occasionally, a musician will venture to the lakeside, draw forth a bamboo flute from their person, and from across the waters, join in a passage of song. Humans and otters disturb each other not, yet in the dusk and notes between them achieve a tacit resonance that transcends species.
What is curious is that this harmonious melody is not without reason. The communal law of the Opus Otters is accompanied by something altogether distinctive: a "stern scrutiny."
A young Opus Otter, it seems, yearns to display itself. It shatters the original languid rhythm, beginning to strike wildly and without pattern. The sharp, chaotic sounds and coarse cries cause the other Opus Otters to exhibit a strikingly anthropomorphic stress response.
They cease their performance, discarding the pebbles and shells in their grasp, raising their forepaws to clap tightly over their ears, even squeezing their eyes shut as if bracing against a sudden tempest. Several of the Opus Otters, pushed to their limit, rush toward this "troublemaker of the colony," using the Opus Stone upon their belly to butt against it, putting an end to the noise.
Under the protest and pressure of the group, this "rule-breaking" individual has no choice but to slink shamefully to the periphery. In the world of the Opus Otters, consensus around the harmonious melody is the secret bond that maintains their survival order.
Adults often point toward the riverbank, seizing the moment to teach the befuddled children at their side:
"See that? If you're trying to show off and cause a ruckus, even these Opus Otters will butt you out the door!"
